label: Town of Windsor
header:
# Town of Windsor municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 28; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 173 (Town of Windsor): sec. 11 (Subchapter 003) elects a five-member selectboard: three members for three-year terms and two for two-year terms

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): names Tera Howard (Chair), Emma Caffrey (Vice Chair), Jeffrey Johnson, Mary McNaughton, and Heather Prebish for Windsor

Town of Windsor, Selectboard page (live): the same five members with term expiries -- Howard (2029), Johnson (2028), McNaughton (2028), Caffrey (2027), Prebish (2027); Howard's 2029 expiry reflects his 2026 re-election

Town of Windsor, official sample ballot, March 3, 2026 (DocumentCenter/View/2524): the printed 2026 selectboard contests -- the three-year seat and two two-year seats (one contested: Jeffrey Johnson over Eric Saltonstall)
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 173 (Town of Windsor): sec. 11 elects a town clerk for a three-year term
Town of Windsor, Warning for the March 3, 2026 annual town meeting (DocumentCenter/View/2508): the 2026 ballot carried Town Clerk for the one-year remainder of a three-year term

Town of Windsor, official sample ballot, March 3, 2026 (DocumentCenter/View/2524): the clerk contest printed no candidate -- write-in only. No certified tally or current roster naming the winner is published, so no holder is minted; the office's history is carried as a straggler on issue #163

Town of Windsor, FY2023-24 Annual Town Report (DocumentCenter/View/1956): Jane Mayhew held clerk (and treasurer) to 2027 and departed before the 2026 meeting, which is why a remainder term stood on the 2026 ballot
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 173 (Town of Windsor): sec. 11 elects a town treasurer for a three-year term; the treasurer is ex officio collector of current and delinquent taxes
Town of Windsor, Warning for the March 3, 2026 annual town meeting (DocumentCenter/View/2508): the 2026 ballot carried Town Treasurer for the one-year remainder of a three-year term

Town of Windsor, official sample ballot, March 3, 2026 (DocumentCenter/View/2524): the treasurer contest printed no candidate -- write-in only. No certified tally or current roster naming the winner is published, so no holder is minted; the office is carried as a straggler on issue #163
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): shows Windsor's treasurer seat as vacant
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 173 (Town of Windsor): sec. 11 elects a moderator for a one-year term

Town of Windsor, official sample ballot, March 3, 2026 (DocumentCenter/View/2524): the moderator contest printed no candidate -- write-in only. No certified tally or current roster naming the winner is published, so no holder is minted; the office is carried as a straggler on issue #163
Town of Windsor, FY2023-24 Annual Town Report (DocumentCenter/View/1956): the moderator line printed vacant
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 173 (Town of Windsor): sec. 11 elects three listers
Town of Windsor, Warning for the March 3, 2026 annual town meeting (DocumentCenter/View/2508): the 2026 ballot carried three lister seats

Town of Windsor, official sample ballot, March 3, 2026 (DocumentCenter/View/2524): the lister contests printed no candidates -- write-in only. No certified tally or current roster naming the winners is published, so no holders are minted; the seats are carried as stragglers on issue #163
Town of Windsor, FY2023-24 Annual Town Report (DocumentCenter/View/1956): the lister lines printed vacant

jp_election.name: Town of Windsor Justice of the Peace Election 2024-11-05

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): certifies the November 5, 2024 election of twelve justices of the peace for Windsor: William Ballantyne, Paul Belaski, Marianne N Blake, Janet Farley, Linda Farnsworth, Patricia Crikett French, Steve Giroux, Amy McMullen, David Morin, Sara Morin, Ryan Palmer, and Donna Sweaney. Ryan Palmer is Windsor County's elected sheriff; his existing county-tier record is reused and the JP candidacy is appended to it
